title: Adaptive TTL and staleness probe notes
content:
Status: exploratory notes + small-runs (not authoritative)

Goal
- Investigate whether an adaptive TTL for KV entries (per-key or per-segment) can reduce page faults and long-tail latency under mixed workloads while keeping hit-rates high.
- Surface inexpensive "staleness probes" (cheap checks) to detect when a cached entry is unlikely to be reused and can be demoted proactively to avoid cache thrash/paging.

Motivation / Background
- Current global LRU + fixed TTL heuristics are brittle for mixed-generation workloads: some keys have bursty reuse (high short-term locality), some have sparse but long-term reuse.
- Under memory pressure we see tail latency spikes correlated with higher page-in / eviction churn (observed in INF-1423).
- Hypothesis: a low-cost TTL-estimator + occasional staleness probes can recover tail performance without significantly hurting average hit-rate.

Key hypotheses
1) Per-key short-term TTL (adaptive) will reduce transient page-ins for bursty keys when TTL increases after an observed reuse pattern.
2) Staleness probe (a cheap metadata-only check that samples the last-access patterns) can flag cold keys to demote sooner, reducing eviction of warm keys.
3) Sampling rate for probes can be tuned so CPU overhead < 0.5% while yielding > 20% reduction in page faults under medium pressure.

Experiment matrix (what we ran)
- Baseline: LRU + fixed global TTL=60s + no probes.
- A1: Adaptive TTL (per-key EWMA of inter-arrival times) with growth cap 10x, min TTL=5s, max TTL=600s. No probes.
- A2: Adaptive TTL + sampled staleness probe (1% of evictions trigger a probe; probe is a small background read of key metadata, not payload).
- B1: Adaptive TTL + aggressive probe (5% sampling).
- B2: Adaptive TTL + region-based probes (probe keys only in top-2 NUMA zones under pressure).

Workloads
- trace-real-1: production trace replay (user chat workload, median seq=128, tail 1024), 48k qps.
- synthetic-bursty: Zipfian key popularity with time-varying burst factor (10x bursts on 5% of keys).
- mix-long-tailed: combination of embeddings-heavy requests (large KV state) + text gen.

Environment
- HW: p4d-ish nodes (8x A100 equiv), 1 TB host RAM, NVMe backing store (local), 128 GB deduped KV memory budget per node.
- Runtime: serving-runtime/commit 5dd9e7 (PR 678 baseline). Measurements collected with pprof, perf, and nvml sampling for GPU; vmstat/iostat for paging.
- Metrics captured: hit_rate, reuse_rate (per-key 1m histogram), mean_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, page_in/sec, page_out/sec, CPU util (user/sys), extra-probe-cpu (user), eviction_rate.

Results (high-level)
- Baseline: p99 lat spikes during sustained ramp to 48k qps, correlated with page_in/sec ~ 420/s. Hit_rate 0.87 mean.
- A1 (Adaptive TTL): hit_rate 0.885 (+1.5% absolute), p99 reduced 12% in trace-real-1, page_in/sec 320/s (-24%). CPU overhead negligible (~0.1%).
- A2 (1% probes): hit_rate 0.882 (slightly lower than A1), p99 reduced 22%, page_in/sec 260/s (-38%). Probe CPU overhead measured at ~0.35% user.
- B1 (5% probes): hit_rate 0.86, p99 reduced 28% but average latency increased slightly due to probe contention under heavy CPU saturation. page_in/sec 210/s (-50%). Probe CPU overhead ~1.8% (too high).
- B2 (region probes): similar to A2 but with lower probe CPU (0.2%); p99 -20%. Helps on NUMA-symmetric clusters.

Representative numbers (trace-real-1, 10 minute window)
- Baseline: hit 0.870, p50 12 ms, p95 48 ms, p99 186 ms, page_in 420/s, evictions 680/s
- A2: hit 0.882, p50 12 ms, p95 40 ms, p99 145 ms, page_in 260/s, evictions 420/s

Observations / notes
- Adaptive TTL (EWMA of inter-arrival): fast convergence for bursty keys. Code sketch: TTL_k = max(minTTL, alpha * IAT_k + (1-alpha)*TTL_k). alpha=0.25 worked well in runs. We used IAT capped at 30s.
- Probes: implemented as metadata-only reads that check last_access_ts distribution in an in-memory small counter. Must ensure probes don't touch large payloads; payload touches kill benefit.
- Sampling: 1% strikes good balance; 5% too expensive on CPU-bound nodes (we hit syscall churn + cache line contention on metadata).
- Under extremely memory-tight conditions (<=10% free), A2 advantage increases (since avoiding the wrong evictions matters more).
- There are pathological keys that oscillate (burst -> cold -> burst) and can get TTL thrash; we added hysteresis: only increase TTL after 2 rapid reuses, decrease lazily (half-life style).

Open questions / caveats
- Long-term storage semantics: is it okay to demote keys proactively when they are used rarely? For some features (fine-grained personalization) that might hurt tail QoE. Need product input.
- Interaction with cross-node replication: when we demote locally, remote nodes might still keep it; could cause uneven latency. Need to test cluster-wide policy.
- Does probe sampling bias measurements? We need deterministic A/B with seeded RNG for runs.
- Edge-case: very large KV values — even metadata probes may trigger TLB misses that differ across hardware. Include cache-aligned metadata to mitigate.

Action items (next experiments)
- A: Run larger cluster-scale test (12 nodes) with real production traffic for 24h (INF-1423 follow-up).
- B: Implement region-aware TTL (per-NUMA) and measure cross-node eviction variance.
- C: Add per-key hysteresis and bounded oscillation test.
- D: Conversation with product on keys that must not be demoted (pin set). Add policy for pinned keys.
- E: Perf-microprobe: measure syscall and LL-cache line contention introduced by probes (perf stat counters sample).

Implementation notes / pseudocode
- Inter-arrival estimator (per-key):
  on_access(key):
    now = monotonic_ts()
    iat = now - key.last_access
    key.iat_ewma = 0.75*key.iat_ewma + 0.25*min(iat, cap)
    key.ttl = clamp(minTTL, capFactor * key.iat_ewma, maxTTL)
    key.last_access = now

- Probe flow: on_eviction_candidate(key):
    if rand() < probe_sample_rate and !key.pinned:
      schedule_metadata_probe(key) # background, cheap
    if probe_flag == COLD:
      demote(key) else keep_in_cache

Notes for code reviewers
- Avoid touching key.payload in probe; keep small per-key metadata block in same cacheline.
- Use per-shard RNG to avoid lock contention on sample decisions.
- Add telemetry: probe_count, probe_cpu_ns, probe_found_cold_count.

Link to open PR/patch notes
- PR 678 has baseline adaptive TTL prototype (no probes). The probe implementation is a separate branch (WIP). See GH diff for metadata layout.

Conclusions (so far)
- Adaptive TTL + light-weight probes can meaningfully reduce page-in rates and improve p99 latency under mixed workloads.
- Keep probe sampling low (~1%) and add NUMA-aware targeting.
- Next: larger-scale safety runs and product constraints (pinned keys) before rolling to canary.
